classification.difficultyReason: Derive symbolic tangent equations and connect their intersection with the vertex of a general quadratic.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the tangents at the $x$-intercepts have opposite gradients.

answer.short: $m_\alpha=k(\alpha-\beta)$ and $m_\beta=-k(\alpha-\beta)$, so the gradients are opposite.
answer.worked:
The intercepts are at $x=\alpha$ and $x=\beta$.

At $x=\alpha$:
$$\begin{aligned}m_\alpha&=k(2\alpha-\alpha-\beta)\\&=k(\alpha-\beta).\end{aligned}$$
At $x=\beta$:
$$\begin{aligned}m_\beta&=k(2\beta-\alpha-\beta)\\&=k(\beta-\alpha)\\&=-k(\alpha-\beta).\end{aligned}$$
Therefore the tangents at the intercepts have opposite gradients.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show the tangents meet at point $M$ whose $x$-coordinate is the average of the $x$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
Tangent at $(\alpha,0)$:
$$y=k(\alpha-\beta)(x-\alpha).$$
Tangent at $(\beta,0)$:
$$y=-k(\alpha-\beta)(x-\beta).$$
At their intersection:
$$\begin{aligned}k(\alpha-\beta)(x-\alpha)&=-k(\alpha-\beta)(x-\beta)\\x-\alpha&=-x+\beta\\2x&=\alpha+\beta\\x&=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus the tangents at the intercepts meet at the average of the intercepts.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the point $V$ where the tangent is horizontal.

answer.worked:
The tangent is horizontal when
$$\begin{aligned}k(2x-\alpha-\beta)&=0\\2x-\alpha-\beta&=0\\2x&=\alpha+\beta\\x&=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Substitute into the parabola equation:
$$\begin{aligned}y_V&=k\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}-\alpha\right)\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}-\beta\right)\\&=k\left(\frac{\beta-\alpha}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}\right)\\&=-\frac{k(\alpha-\beta)^2}{4}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $V=\left(\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2},-\dfrac{k(\alpha-\beta)^2}{4}\right)$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Show that $M$ is vertically above or below $V$ and twice as far from the $x$-axis.

answer.worked:
$M$ and $V$ have the same $x$-coordinate, so one lies vertically above the other.

Substitute $x=\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}$ into either tangent equation:
$$\begin{aligned}y_M&=k(\alpha-\beta)\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}-\alpha\right)\\&=k(\alpha-\beta)\frac{\beta-\alpha}{2}\\&=-\frac{k(\alpha-\beta)^2}{2}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $M=\left(\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2},-\dfrac{k(\alpha-\beta)^2}{2}\right)$.

The $y$-coordinate of $M$ is twice that of $V$. Therefore $|y_M|=2|y_V|$, so $M$ is twice as far from the $x$-axis.

spec.description: Illustrative upward-opening parabola in blue and its two intercept tangents in red. The vertex V and tangent intersection M share a vertical line slightly left of the y-axis. Both axes and all curve ends are arrowed. No numerical ticks or intercept labels.
spec.mathematics: For a nondegenerate quadratic with distinct real roots, x_M=x_V=(alpha+beta)/2 and y_M=2y_V. Internal drawing coordinates illustrate the relationship and are not numerical givens.
